source: MAFF — សារៈប្រយោជន៍នៃដំណាំស្រូវ (Value of the Rice Crop) slide deck, presenter contact temseng@yahoo.com, p.11
text: Rice bran — the nutrient-rich outer layer of the rice grain removed during milling/polishing — can be processed into rice bran cooking oil, a value-added product made from what is otherwise a milling byproduct. The slide shows a commercial example (brand 'ARROZA,' labeled '100% Rice Bran Oil, Cooking and Salad Oil') with claimed properties: Oryzanol content of 2500 ppm, contains Vitamin E, has a high smoke point (suitable for high-heat frying), no cholesterol, no preservatives, non-GMO, and 0% trans fat; marketed as suitable for frying, baking, and salads. This illustrates rice bran oil as a premium, health-marketed cooking oil that millers or processors could produce from bran instead of discarding or selling it cheaply as animal feed.
